# script to calculate date between to git commits

Add a helper that reports the time between two commits, or between a commit and now. The ingredients noted:

```
- `git rev-list -n 1 release-202201111351`
- `git show --no-patch --no-notes --pretty='%cI' 24214c334e9416b52d0dc67c3140c25f10893a56 | cat`
- `date +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"`
- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4946785/how-to-find-the-difference-in-days-between-two-dates/6948865
```

i.e. resolve a tag or ref to a commit, take its committer date, and compute the difference in days (and hours/minutes) against another date. The context is the dated-commit tooling — `git at` takes an offset, so the offset that corresponds to "the commit before the release" has to be computed.

my solution
```
  # verification step
  local latest
  latest=$(info releases | head -1)
  echo Please check errors at staging and verify the diff first.
    # actual hours
    local commit gnu prev hours
    local fmt='s|release-([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})|\1-\2-\3 \4:\5 UTC|'
    commit=$(git rev-list -n 1 "${latest}")
    gnu=$(echo "${latest}" | sed -r "${fmt}")
    prev=$(date -u -jf 'release-%Y%m%d%H%M' "${latest}" +%s || date -u -d "${gnu}" +%s)
    hours="$(( $(($(date -u +%s) - prev)) / (60*60) ))h"
```
